WoW: Forever · Updated October 8, 2026 · Beta build 1.60.1.70245 · Null Ossuary

Written for levelling, 1 to 60. Forever's beta is capped at level 30 as of the October 1 build, which Blizzard raised from 20 that day, so no level-60 Mage build has been tested. Ability training levels below come from foreverchanges.pro's reading of the beta client. Caster base damage was cut across the board and spell coefficients raised to compensate, so a lower tooltip number than Classic is usually not a nerf. Neither Wowhead nor ClassicWoW.gg publishes a levelling score for the three specs. Icy Veins is the only one of the three that rates them, giving each a number out of five and a heading; those appear on each spec's own page. Blizzard's caveat covers its October 7 deep dive throughout: "class abilities and talents may continue to evolve throughout the beta test and are subject to additional changes."

The three specs do different things, and Blizzard frames the pick as three answers to the same weakness: "Arcane to manipulate and consume Mana for more damage. Fire to produce devastatingly heavy hits and critical damage. Or Frost to grant levels of combat control still unrivaled by any other class." Each spec page carries Icy Veins' score and heading.

No source confirms or denies a target cap or damage falloff on Mage area spells in Forever, and Blizzard's deep dive does not mention one either.

The slows attached to area damage were cut hard, and Blizzard says why. Improved BlizzardImproved BlizzardTalentCastInstantAdds a Chill effect to your Blizzard spell. This effect lowers the target's movement speed by 40% for 1.5 sec. now maxes at 40%, down from 65%, to stop Frost Mages farming instances, "which was widely used by gold farmers and boosters to disrupt the economy of the game." Cone of ColdCone of ColdSpell · Frost · Rank 1 of 5CastInstantCost120 ManaCooldown10 sec cooldownDuration8 secInflicts Frost damage to enemies in a cone in front of the caster, reducing their movement speed for 8 sec.'s duration was shortened for the same reason.

Is Mage for you?

Play Mage if you want burst damage from range and can accept cloth armour, no self-heal and a mana bar you have to manage. (Our own reading, not a source's.)

Blizzard's own summary gives both halves. Mages "remain one of the most powerful and resourceful damage dealing classes" and "masters of ranged area damage which is stronger and more varied than any other class". They are also "extremely fragile and die easily if caught in melee combat", and the spec you pick is how you answer that.

New to this class?

Is the rotation simple? The published level 20 rotations run five or six steps: a nuke, a freeze, a retreat, a wand finish.

Is it forgiving? No. You have cloth armour, no self-heal, and mana that does not regenerate while you cast.

What carries you while levelling? Conjured drink from level 4 and food from level 6, so you buy neither. PolymorphPolymorphLevel 8 · Spell · Arcane · Rank 1 of 4Cast1.5 sec castCost60 ManaRange30 yd rangeDuration20 secTransforms the enemy into a sheep, forcing it to wander around for up to 20 sec. While wandering, the sheep cannot attack or cast spells but will regenerate very quickly. Any damage will transform the target back into its normal form. Only one target can be polymorphed at a time. Only works on Beasts, Humanoids and Critters. from 8 takes one enemy out of a fight.

Does it need a group? No. Every spec has a published solo build, and Arcane and Frost also have published dungeon variants.

Frostfire BoltFrostfire BoltLevel 40 · Spell · Rank 1 of 3Cast3 sec castCost205 ManaRange35 yd rangeDuration9 secLaunches a bolt of frostfire at the enemy, causing 100 Frostfire damage, slowing movement speed by 40% and causing an additional 27 Frostfire damage over 9 sec. This spell will be checked against the lower of the target's Frost and Fire resists and counts as both Frost and Fire damage. counts as both a Fire and a Frost spell: it takes the higher of your two spell damage bonuses and the lower of the target's two resistances. Its 3-second cast lands Fireball-sized damage plus a damage-over-time and a slow, and Blizzard's stated intent is to make mixed Frost-and-Fire builds work. It is learned at 40, above the beta cap, so nobody has cast it.

Which race

Read this section in proportion. Race is the smallest choice on this page, well behind spec, gear and knowing your rotation, and no race is a wrong answer for levelling (ours, not a source's). Racials decide things in PvP. The ones that matter there break crowd control: Will of the ForsakenWill of the ForsakenTalentCastInstantCooldown120 sec cooldownInstantly removes all Charm, Fear and Sleep effects. (Undead, fear, sleep and charm), Escape ArtistEscape ArtistTalentCastInstantCooldown120 sec cooldownDuration3 secInstantly escape the effects of any movement impairing effect and gain immunity to those effects for 3 sec. (Gnome, roots and snares) and StoneformStoneformTalentCastInstantCooldown180 sec cooldownDuration8 secInstantly removes and grants immunity to all Bleed, Poison, and Disease effects, and reduces all Physical damage taken by 10% for 8 sec. (Dwarf, bleeds, poisons and disease). A free trinket slot is worth more than any damage racial below.

Alliance — Human or Gnome. Human's Sword SpecializationSword SpecializationTalent · Rank 1 of 14CastInstantDurationUntil cancelledIncreases your critical strike chance with all spells and attacks by 2% while you have a sword or two-handed sword equipped. gives +2% spell and ability crit off a sword held purely as a stat stick, a real change from the vanilla answer. Compare it against a staff with better stats anyway: at levelling levels the staff often wins. Gnome brings Expansive MindExpansive MindTalentCastInstantMaximum Mana increased by 5%. and Eureka!Eureka!TalentCastInstantCooldown120 sec cooldownDuration15 secYour next 3 damaging abilities have their Mana cost reduced by 10% and deal 10% more damage.. Blizzard's October 1 notes made Eureka!Eureka!TalentCastInstantCooldown120 sec cooldownDuration15 secYour next 3 damaging abilities have their Mana cost reduced by 10% and deal 10% more damage. a flat 10% cost discount on every class. The Mage's own client entry covers your next 3 damaging abilities and carries no periodic restriction, where other classes' copies of it exclude periodic effects. A channeled cast like Arcane MissilesArcane MissilesLevel 8 · Spell · Arcane · Rank 1 of 8CastInstantCost85 ManaRange30 yd rangeDuration3 secLaunches Arcane Missiles at the enemy, causing 24 Arcane damage each second for 3 sec. or EvocationEvocationLevel 20 · Spell · ArcaneCastInstantCooldown480 sec cooldownDuration8 secWhile channeling this spell, your mana regeneration is active and increased by 1500%. Lasts 8 sec. benefits either way; whether a damage-over-time tick such as Fire's IgniteIgniteTalentCastInstantYour critical strikes from Fire damage spells cause the target to burn for an additional 40% of your spell's damage over 4 sec. does is unsettled. (Known issue: Eureka currently doesn't affect every damaging or healing spell for some classes; Blizzard says it's fixed in a later build.)

Horde — Orc is new to Mage in Forever. Blood FuryBlood FuryTalentCastInstantCooldown120 sec cooldownDuration15 secIncreases Attack Power and Spell Power by 10% for 15 sec. now gives +10% spell power, so it is finally a caster racial. Its axe racial is dead weight: Mages cannot use axes.

Skyborne Mage is Alliance-only. Troll's BerserkingBerserkingTalentCastInstantCooldown180 sec cooldownDuration10 sec is now a flat +10% cast speed, and Undead's CannibalizeCannibalizeTalentCastInstantRangeMeleeCooldown120 sec cooldownWhen activated, regenerates 7% of total Health and 7% of total Mana every 2 sec for 10 sec. Only works on Humanoid or Undead corpses within 5 yds. Any movement, action, or damage taken while Cannibalizing will cancel the effect. restores mana as well as health.

Quality of life

  • Conjured water is free drink from level 4, upgrading through the gem ladder, so there is never a reason to buy it.
  • Teleports come from a separate portal trainer standing near your class trainer, and every teleport consumes a Rune of Teleportation at about nine and a half silver. Slow FallSlow FallLevel 12 · Spell · ArcaneCastInstantCost40 ManaDuration30 secSlows falling speed for 30 sec. eats a Light Feather per cast, so carry a stack of both.
  • Loot scrolls, and pick up books from level 6. Blizzard calls Comprehension a Mage-only minor tradeskill for deciphering scrolls dropped by creatures, and leaves the rewards for "players to discover in their adventures". Comprehend ScrollComprehend ScrollSpell · PhysicalCastInstantRangeMeleeDecipher an untranslated scroll. sits in the General tab of your spellbook, and failing to decipher a scroll turns you into a sheep until your skill improves. The separate Research system is described by the guide sites and the client, and absent from Blizzard's deep dive. It unlocks from finding books in the world and returning them to librarians, and pays a ring for twenty donations and a pendant from its quest. (Known issue, October 1: some Mages who learn Research find themselves locked out of accessing it. That is a bug, not something you did; check it works before you chase Research early.)
  • Comprehension scrolls cannot be cast while moving. Budget the stand-still time like any other cast.
  • Get a wand early and use it instead of Fire BlastFire BlastLevel 6 · Spell · Fire · Rank 1 of 7CastInstantCost40 ManaRange20 yd rangeCooldown8 sec cooldownBlasts the enemy for 28 Fire damage..
  • Respeccing means a class trainer in a major city, Blizzard's stated route for Legacy talents too. Dual Specialization arrives at level 40, above the beta cap and untested; below it you pay for every reset.

At level 60

Unknown. No source publishes a Mage build past 30. Whether Arcane's new engine holds up, whether Fire takes over once Pyroblast is usable, and how far the scroll system goes are all untested. Raids open December 9.
